entries.title: Mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
entries.summary: Three mutually unbiased bases are known in dimension six. Neither a fourth basis nor an accepted proof excluding a complete set of seven is known.

latestEvidence.title: Peer-reviewed composite-dimension review keeps the case open

entries.title: NPT bound entanglement
entries.summary: No negative-partial-transpose state has been proved undistillable for every finite number of copies.

latestEvidence.title: A candidate family is two-copy distillable in every dimension

entries.title: SIC POVMs in infinitely many dimensions
entries.summary: Exact SICs are known in many individual dimensions, but no unconditional construction covers an infinite sequence of dimensions.

latestEvidence.title: Claimed all-dimension proof was withdrawn

entries.title: Classify all Bell inequalities
entries.summary: Facet lists are complete only for small scenarios or restricted correlation spaces. No closed-form classification exists for arbitrary parties, settings and outcomes.

latestEvidence.title: Polyhedral sampling scales by giving up completeness

entries.title: Bell inequalities for long-range vacuum correlations
entries.summary: Vacuum entanglement persists at arbitrary separation, but direct CHSH violation by bounded distant regions has not been proved or excluded.

latestEvidence.title: Arbitrary-distance harvesting reveals hidden nonlocality

entries.title: Catalytic majorization
entries.summary: Trumping has exact necessary-and-sufficient characterizations by infinite families of inequalities, but no finite efficient test comparable to Nielsen's partial-sum criterion is known.

latestEvidence.title: A finite sufficient criterion is available

entries.title: The power of CGLMP inequalities
entries.summary: The proposed facet completeness is false. The claimed necessity and simultaneous optimality of Fourier-plus-diagonal measurements remain open.

latestEvidence.title: Part A is refuted by a finite facet counterexample

entries.title: Complexity of product preparations
entries.summary: No general asymptotic formula is known for the weighted Pauli-rotation cost of preparing many copies of a pure state.

latestEvidence.title: The archived weighted-cost problem remains unresolved

entries.title: Entanglement of formation for Gaussian states
entries.summary: Gaussian and unrestricted entanglement of formation now coincide for every two-mode Gaussian state and for bisymmetric multimode states. Generic nonsymmetric multimode states remain open.

latestEvidence.title: All two-mode Gaussian states are settled

entries.title: Lockability of two-way distillable entanglement and key
entries.summary: Several nearby measures and one-way distillable entanglement are lockable, but the requested two-way distillable entanglement and arbitrary-state distillable key questions remain unresolved.

latestEvidence.title: Non-lockability is proved for irreducible private states

entries.title: Mutually unbiased bases in general dimensions
entries.summary: Complete sets exist in prime-power dimensions, but the maximum number is unknown in general composite dimensions. Dimension six is the first unresolved case.

latestEvidence.title: Current review confirms the composite-dimension gap

entries.title: Two-qubit relative entropy of entanglement
entries.summary: Special families and an inverse closest-separable-state construction are known, but no closed formula covers every two-qubit mixed state.

latestEvidence.title: The inverse closest-state problem is solved

entries.title: Reversible entanglement manipulation
entries.summary: Universal reversibility under PPT operations is false, and irreversibility survives even for exact non-entangling maps. The smallest meaningful reversible operation class is unknown.

latestEvidence.title: Exact non-entangling maps remain irreversible

entries.title: Secret key from every entangled state
entries.summary: Many entangled states, including PPT examples, have positive distillable key. No proof covers every entangled state, and no entangled state is known with proved zero distillable key.

latestEvidence.title: Current key-cost theory still treats zero-key entanglement as unresolved

entries.title: Separability from spectrum
entries.summary: Absolute separability is characterized for every 2-by-n system. A complete spectral criterion is unknown when both local dimensions are at least three.

latestEvidence.title: A 4-by-n claim proves APPT, not absolute separability

entries.title: SIC POVMs and Zauner's conjecture
entries.summary: Unconditional SIC existence, Weyl-Heisenberg-covariant existence and Zauner-symmetric existence remain unproved in arbitrary dimension.

latestEvidence.title: An unconditional proof claim was withdrawn as incorrect

entries.title: Tough error models
entries.summary: The universal correctable-code lower bound scales as n/e^4, while a simple worst-case upper bound scales as n/e. The gap is not closed.

latestEvidence.title: A structure-free lower bound is proved

entries.title: Does undistillability imply PPT?
entries.summary: The converse of PPT implies undistillable is unresolved in general finite dimensions. This is equivalent to the NPT bound-entanglement problem.

latestEvidence.title: Selected NPT candidates fail at two copies

entries.title: Tightness of metrology bounds under correlated noise
entries.summary: Block-comb semidefinite programs bound the asymptotic precision under correlated noise, but no theorem shows that the best block bound equals the precision of a physical protocol.

latestEvidence.title: The block hierarchy tightens without a convergence theorem

entries.title: Asymptotic metrology with quantum-controlled causal order
entries.summary: Quantum-controlled causal order improves quantum Fisher information for some noisy channels at three uses. Its advantage at large numbers of channel uses remains unknown.

latestEvidence.title: A spacetime theorem identifies QC-QC as the physical target class

entries.title: Delayed-onset additivity violation
entries.summary: No channel is known to be additive for every tensor power below a chosen m at least three, then first become nonadditive at m copies.

latestEvidence.title: Explicit self-channel violations expose a quantifier trap

entries.title: CB entropy of multiplicativity counterexamples
entries.summary: Known examples are consistent with the proposed completely bounded entropy or coherent-information conditions, but no theorem covers every multiplicativity counterexample.

latestEvidence.title: Completely bounded norms give forward additivity implications

entries.title: Audenaert-Ruskai decompositions of CPT maps
entries.summary: The strong equal-weight conjecture holds for every qubit-input channel, cq and qc channels, and a positive-measure set in all dimensions. The weak form holds for qutrit endomorphisms.

latestEvidence.title: Large channel classes satisfy the conjectured decomposition

entries.title: Extreme CPT maps beyond qubit input
entries.summary: Higher-dimensional low-rank classifications and a general fixed-rank quotient parameterization now exist, but no qubit-style canonical classification covers arbitrary dimensions.

latestEvidence.title: Fixed-rank channels receive a quotient-manifold parameterization

entries.title: Local invariants and N-representability
entries.summary: Graph-indexed complete invariant families and a free stable invariant algebra are known. A finite-dimensional minimal set for arbitrary mixed two-particle states and the full N-representability constraints remain unknown.

latestEvidence.title: The stable invariant algebra has graph-indexed generators

entries.title: Channel classes with multiplicativity at p = 2
entries.summary: Many nontrivial channel classes have multiplicative maximal output 2-norm, including PPT-inducing channels tensored with arbitrary channels. No exhaustive characterization exists.

latestEvidence.title: PPT-inducing channels form a broad positive class

entries.title: Nontrivial mutually degradable channel pairs
entries.summary: Trivial identity and identical-degradable pairs exist, but no distinct genuinely nontrivial pair of the intended kind has been identified.

latestEvidence.title: Structural theory sharply constrains degradable channels

entries.title: New extreme CPT classes with additivity
entries.summary: New families of extreme channels have been studied since 2007, but no decisive new structured class with the requested additivity theorem has been located.

latestEvidence.title: New extreme channel families do not supply the requested theorem

entries.title: Polarized near-maximally-mixed channels
entries.summary: General random-channel counterexamples do not settle the polarized family xI + (1-x)M_epsilon or give the requested parameter bounds.

latestEvidence.title: Random-channel violations motivate but do not settle the family

entries.title: Coherent information of random sub-unitary channels
entries.summary: No complete degradability, coherent-information or capacity analysis is known for the intended normalized cyclic sub-unitary family.

latestEvidence.title: Bounded-Schmidt-rank tools address only the surrounding structure

entries.title: Counterexamples among random sub-unitary channels
entries.summary: General random channels violate multiplicativity, but no verified new counterexample has been found inside the intended cyclic sub-unitary family.

latestEvidence.title: Unrestricted random channels violate entropy additivity

entries.title: Maximally entangled relative maxima for sub-unitary channels
entries.summary: The maximally entangled input is analytically understood only in the Werner-Holevo special case. No theorem covers arbitrary unitaries in the intended family.

latestEvidence.title: The Werner-Holevo critical point is a special case only

entries.title: Random sub-unitary multiplicativity at p = 2
entries.summary: General 2-norm multiplicativity is false, but no proof or counterexample settles the intended random sub-unitary subclass.

latestEvidence.title: The closest positive theorem concerns another family

entries.title: A direct proof for the two-Pauli qubit channel
entries.summary: Multiplicativity for this channel follows from King's unital-qubit theorem, but that proof uses exactly the negative-multiplier equivalence that the problem asks to avoid.

latestEvidence.title: A nearby entropy proof does not establish the requested norm theorem

entries.title: Polarized Werner-Holevo multiplicativity
entries.summary: The identical polarized family is settled at p equals two, and the unpolarized endpoint is settled for one through two. The full polarized parameter range remains open.

latestEvidence.title: Every polarization is settled at p = 2

entries.title: Kashaev volume conjecture for hyperbolic knots
entries.summary: Kashaev's quantum knot invariant is conjectured to grow at a rate fixed by the hyperbolic volume of the knot complement.

latestEvidence.title: The universal hyperbolic-knot statement remains open

entries.title: Yang-Mills existence and mass gap
entries.summary: Mathematics lacks a construction of nontrivial four-dimensional quantum Yang-Mills theory satisfying the official axioms together with a proof of a positive mass gap.

latestEvidence.title: Clay continues to list the problem as unsolved

entries.title: Quantum PCP conjecture
entries.summary: Inverse-polynomial-gap Local Hamiltonian is QMA-complete. It is unknown whether QMA-hardness persists when the energy gap is a fixed fraction of the number of terms.

latestEvidence.title: Quantum-PCP reductions leave constant-gap hardness open

entries.title: Determine whether there exist two quantum orthogonal Latin squares of order six (quantum 36 officers of Euler)
entries.summary: The source asked whether two orthogonal quantum Latin squares of order six exist, the quantum version of Euler's problem of 36 officers. Rather and coauthors settled it affirmatively with an exact AME(4,6) construction.

latestEvidence.title: Explicit AME(4,6) state solves the 36 entangled officers

entries.title: Show that the Werner state rho(4, -1/2) of two ququarts is not 2-copy distillable
entries.summary: The source asked for a proof that the two-ququart Werner state rho(4,-1/2) is not 2-copy distillable. Fu, Gao and Park, together with three concurrent teams, proved that a Werner state is 2-copy distillable only if it is already 1-copy distillable, which covers this state.

latestEvidence.title: Werner states are 2-copy distillable only if 1-copy distillable

entries.title: Additivity of classical capacity and related problems
entries.summary: The source asked to prove that the Holevo quantity is additive for every pair of quantum channels or to give an explicit counterexample. Hastings' random-unitary counterexample, combined with Shor's equivalences, showed that additivity fails.

latestEvidence.title: Hastings disproves additivity of the Holevo capacity

entries.title: Additivity of Entanglement of Formation
entries.summary: The source asked to show that the entanglement of formation is additive on tensor products of arbitrary bipartite states. Shor's chain of equivalences together with Hastings' minimal-output-entropy counterexample shows it is strictly subadditive for some pairs.

latestEvidence.title: Hastings counterexample refutes additivity of entanglement of formation

entries.title: Asymptotic cloning is state estimation?
entries.summary: The source asked to decide whether the M-to-infinity limit of the optimal N-to-M cloning fidelity equals the optimal measure-and-reprepare fidelity for every input distribution and every N. Bae and Acin, and independently Chiribella and D'Ariano, proved the equality in full generality.

latestEvidence.title: Asymptotic quantum cloning is state estimation

entries.title: Bell inequalities holding for all quantum states
entries.summary: The source asked whether every boundary point of the quantum correlation body outside the no-signalling boundary is reachable with minimal local dimension and complete von Neumann measurements, and whether every proper Bell inequality admits a quantum violation. Both universal claims fail, by Slofstra's dimension lower bounds and by the Guess Your Neighbor's Input inequalities.

latestEvidence.title: Both universal Bell questions have explicit counterexamples

entries.title: Bell violation by tensoring
entries.summary: The source asked for two bipartite states, neither violating any CHSH inequality, whose tensor product does violate CHSH. Navascues and Vertesi gave explicit two-qubit constructions using only direct measurements on the joint state.

latestEvidence.title: Navascues and Vertesi construct CHSH activation by tensoring

entries.title: Continuity of the quantum channel capacity
entries.summary: The source asked whether the unassisted quantum (coherent) capacity is a continuous function of the channel in cb-norm. Leung and Smith proved uniform continuity for channels with fixed finite output dimension, including at zero-capacity channels.

latestEvidence.title: Leung and Smith prove uniform continuity of quantum capacity

entries.title: Local equivalence of graph states
entries.summary: The source asked whether local-unitary equivalence of graph states always reduces to local-Clifford equivalence. Ji, Chen, Wei and Ying disproved the LU = LC conjecture with explicit counterexamples, the smallest from their construction on 27 qubits.

latestEvidence.title: Ji, Chen, Wei and Ying show the LU-LC conjecture is false

entries.title: Maximally entangled mixed states
entries.summary: The source asked whether the Verstraete-Audenaert-De Moor maximally entangled mixed states maximise every entanglement monotone at a fixed two-qubit spectrum. De Vicente proved that for some rank-two spectra no universal maximiser exists.

latestEvidence.title: Maximally entangled mixed states for a fixed spectrum need not exist

entries.title: Nice error bases
entries.summary: The source asked whether every nice error basis is of shift and multiply type. Klappenecker and Roetteler answered negatively by constructing an abstract error group with a non-monomial irreducible representation.

latestEvidence.title: Klappenecker and Roetteler exhibit a non-monomial nice error basis

entries.title: Polynomial entanglement invariants
entries.summary: The source asked whether polynomial entanglement invariants are complete, that is whether agreement of all polynomial invariants forces two states to be related by local unitaries. Sudbery answered affirmatively by applying the Onishchik-Vinberg theorem on orbits of compact linear groups.

latestEvidence.title: Compact-group invariants separate local unitary orbits

entries.title: Qubit bi-negativity
entries.summary: The source asked whether the second partial transpose of the absolute value of a two-qubit state's partial transpose is always positive semidefinite.

latestEvidence.title: The two-qubit bi-negativity conjecture holds

entries.title: Reduction criterion implies majorization?
entries.summary: The source asked whether the reduction criterion implies the majorization inequalities between the global and local spectra of a bipartite state. Hiroshima proved the implication in 2003.

latestEvidence.title: Hiroshima proves the reduction criterion implies majorization

entries.title: Reversibility of entanglement assisted coding
entries.summary: The source asked to prove that entanglement-assisted channel simulation is reversible, so that the rate for simulating T from S is the reciprocal of the rate for simulating S from T. The Quantum Reverse Shannon Theorem of Bennett, Devetak, Harrow, Shor and Winter established the identity.

latestEvidence.title: Quantum Reverse Shannon Theorem gives the reciprocal identity

entries.title: Stronger Bell inequalities for Werner states?
entries.summary: The source asked for a Bell inequality whose set of violating Werner states strictly contains the set violating CHSH. Vertesi constructed inequalities with many binary settings violated by two-qubit Werner states for p above 0.7056, below the CHSH threshold.

latestEvidence.title: Vertesi finds Bell inequalities beating CHSH on Werner states

entries.title: Additivity of minimal output (von Neumann) entropy of quantum channels
entries.summary: The source asked to prove additivity of the minimal output entropy for every pair of quantum channels or to find a counterexample. Hastings constructed random unitary channel pairs with a strict additivity gap, refuting the conjecture in 2009.

latestEvidence.title: Hastings refutes additivity of the minimal output entropy

entries.title: Explicit (non-existential) channels violating multiplicativity of maximal output p-norm for p not equal to 1
entries.summary: The source asked for explicitly given channels, not random existence arguments, violating multiplicativity of the maximal output p-norm at some p different from 1. The Werner-Holevo channel already supplies one for p above 4.79, and Cubitt, Harrow, Leung, Montanaro and Winter later gave an explicit 4-to-3 pair at p = 0.

latestEvidence.title: Werner-Holevo channel is an explicit multiplicativity counterexample

entries.title: Find more counterexamples to multiplicativity (eq. 24); do they support holding for 1 <= p <= 2?
entries.summary: The source asked for multiplicativity counterexamples beyond the Werner-Holevo channel and its perturbations and whether multiplicativity survives for 1 <= p <= 2. Winter gave counterexamples for every p above 2, Hayden extended them to all 1 < p < 2, and Winter subsequently closed p = 2.

latestEvidence.title: Winter and Hayden refute multiplicativity for every p above 1

entries.title: Channel or pair of channels violating p-norm multiplicativity for both some p>1 and some 0<p<1
entries.summary: The source asked whether a single channel or channel pair can violate equation (26) simultaneously at some p above 1 and some p below 1. Hastings' fixed finite-dimensional additivity gap at p = 1, combined with continuity of the minimum output Renyi entropy in p, supplies such a pair.

latestEvidence.title: Hastings gap plus continuity in p gives a two-sided violation
